attachment.content:
- deep-research: Deep research harness — fan-out web searches, fetch sources, adversarially verify claims, synthesize a cited report. - When the user wants a deep, multi-source, fact-checked research report on any topic. BEFORE invoking, check if the question is specific enough to research directly — if underspecified (e.g., "what car to buy" without budget/use-case/region), ask 2-3 clarifying questions to narrow scope. Then pass the refined question as args, weaving the answers in.
- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- verify: Verify that a code change actually does what it's supposed to by exercising it end-to-end and observing behavior — drive the affected flow, not just tests or typecheck. Run before committing nontrivial changes; bootstraps this repo's project verify skill if none exists yet. Don't invoke it on a diff that only touches tests, docs, or other code with no runtime surface to drive (a change to product source always has one) — there's nothing to observe.
- code-review: Review the current diff for correctness bugs and reuse/simplification/efficiency cleanups at the given effort level (low/medium: fewer, high-confidence findings; high→max: broader coverage, may include uncertain findings). Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply the findings to the working tree after the review.
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo, defaults to 10m) - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).
- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).
- init: Initialize a new CLAUDE.md file with codebase documentation
- review: Review a GitHub pull request; for your working diff use /code-review
- security-review: Complete a security review of the pending changes on the current branch

Attacked with the previously-untested other-field shapes: ("http","example.com","80","","?q=1","") -> L5=[?q=1], L7=[http://example.com:80??q=1]; ("","","-1","","?q=1","#f") -> L5=[?q=1], L7=[??q=1##f]; ("http","example.com","80","/","??","##") -> L5=[??], L7=[http://example.com:80/???###]. Machine-checked byte-exact on 13,298 predictions with 0 failures.

CONFIRMED (rule 2) - normalize_query is never invoked by from_components. Attacked with 61 purpose-built normalizer-bait strings x 4 fragment settings x 4 URL shapes (1024 byte-exact checks, 0 failures): 'b=2&a=1', 'c=3&b=2&a=1', 'zzz=1&yyy=2&xxx=3&www=4&vvv=5', '9=1&10=2&1=3' never reorder; 'a=1&a=2&a=3', 'a=1&A=1&a=1' never dedupe; '&', '&&&', 'a=1&&', '&&a=1', 'a=&a=' never drop empty pairs; 'q=a+b', '+' never '+'->' '; 'a=1;b=2', ';' never re-split; 'A=1&a=2', 'MiXeD=CaSe' never case-folded; 'utm_source=x&utm_medium=y&id=1' never filtered. Crucially this held with path="" and with scheme/host both empty, not just the canonical shape.

CONFIRMED (rule 3) - no percent-encoding and no percent-decoding on query. '%2F' vs '%2f' both preserved with case intact; '%41' not decoded to 'A'; 'q=%20' stays, 'q=a b' stays raw (L7=[http://example.com:80/?q=a b]); malformed '%', '%2', '%zz' unrepaired. All 14 structural chars ?#&=%+/;:@space.a1 verified in every 2-character combination (196 strings) as query and as fragment, with and without the other field set: 784 byte-exact checks, 0 failures.

CONFIRMED (rule 4) - '#' inside query is NOT split into fragment and NOT escaped. Attacked with the previously-untested NON-EMPTY fragment: q=[q=1#frag] f=[myfrag] -> L5=[q=1#frag], L6=[myfrag], L7=[http://example.com:80/?q=1#frag#myfrag]; q=[a#b#c] f=[d#e] -> L7=[http://example.com:80/?a#b#c#d#e]; q=[#] f=[#] -> L7=[http://example.com:80/?###]; q=[q=1#] f=[x] -> L7=[http://example.com:80/?q=1##x].

CONFIRMED (rule 5) - fragment is stored verbatim; no '#' strip, no trim, no encode/decode, and a '?' inside fragment is never moved to query. Attacked with the previously-untested NON-EMPTY query: q=[q=1] f=[?x=2] -> L5=[q=1], L6=[?x=2], L7=[http://example.com:80/?q=1#?x=2]; q=[q=1] f=[f?g?h] -> L7=[http://example.com:80/?q=1#f?g?h]; q=[?#] f=[#?] -> L7=[http://example.com:80/??###?].

CONFIRMED (rule 6) - to_string appends ('?'+query) iff query.len()!=0 then ('#'+fragment) iff fragment.len()!=0, and emptiness is pure byte-length-0. od of q=[ ] f=[ ] shows '/ ? sp # sp \n 1' (both separators emitted for space-only). No special-casing of a query that is exactly "?": q=[?] f=[] -> L7=[http://example.com:80/??]. Exact length identity verified: len(L7) == len(base) + (q?1+len(q):0) + (f?1+len(f):0) on every one of 44 length points from 0 to 131071 bytes.

CONFIRMED (rule 7) - order is always base, then ?query, then #fragment; exactly one '?' and one '#' are added by to_string, including when scheme/host/port/path are all empty or elided. Verified over 2,016 wide-shape checks (7 schemes x 4 hosts x 6 ports x 6 paths x 3 q/f settings): ("","","0","","Q","F") -> L7=[?Q#F]; ("","","0","","","F") -> L7=[#F]; ("","","0","","Q","") -> L7=[?Q]; ("","example.com","-1","","Q","F") -> L7=[?Q#F] with L8=1. Fragment never precedes query in any observed run.

CONFIRMED (rule 8) - is_valid ignores query and fragment completely. Byte-exact predictive checks asserted L8 == the L8 of the same shape with q=f="" on all 13,298 runs, including the invalid shapes ("","","0",""), ("","","-1",""), ("http","","-1","") and ("http","","0","") each paired with all 255 single-byte values and 52 nasty strings. No q/f value ever flipped 1->0 or 0->1.

CONFIRMED (rule 9) - arbitrary raw bytes survive byte-for-byte in both fields and in to_string. Extended beyond the original claim to the ENTIRE non-NUL byte space: every byte 0x01..0xFF tested in 6 positions (query alone, fragment alone, both, embedded mid-string 'a<b>b', invalid-URL shape, empty-path shape) = 1,530 byte-exact checks, 0 failures. od confirms: q=[a<TAB>b] -> '? a \t b'; q=[a<LF>b] -> '? a \n b'; q=[a<CR>b] -> '? a \r b'; q=[a\001b] f=[c\037d] -> '? a 001 b # c 037 d'; q=[\177] f=[\013\014] -> '? 177 # \v \f'; q=[q=\377\376] f=[\200f] -> '? q = 377 376 # 200 f'.

CONFIRMED (rule 10) - no length limit or truncation imposed by the binary, and the concatenation length identity is exact. Verified verbatim round-trip at 44 lengths including 4095/4096/4097, 65535/65536/65537, 100000, and the true ceiling 131071: q=131071 'z' + f='F' -> rc=0, L5_len=131071, L7_len=131086, L8=1. The only failure point is the OS, not the library (see newRules).

CONFIRMED (rule 11, strengthened) - the exhaustive machine check holds far beyond printable ASCII. Independent re-derivation using a byte-exact whole-stdout oracle (predict all 8 lines from a base run with q=f="") passed 13,298 cases with 0 failures: 5,194 (52-value cross product + 15 URL shapes), 1,530 (all bytes 0x01-0xFF), 2,500 (random multi-byte fuzz, seeded), 1,024 (normalizer bait), 2,016 (wide shapes), 1,034 (2-char and 3-char structural combinatorics). Output is also deterministic (6 identical runs, same md5) and locale-independent (LC_ALL=C / en_US.UTF-8 / POSIX give identical md5).
newRules: RESOLVES UNCERTAINTY (embedded NUL): NUL is not a library concern - execve truncates the argv C-string at the first NUL, so the library only ever sees the prefix. Evidence: exec(BIN,"http","e","80","/","a\0b","c\0d") -> L5=[a], L6=[c], L7=[http://e:80/?a#c], L8=1. A Rust implementer must model the field as 'bytes up to the first NUL'.

RESOLVES UNCERTAINTY (length ceiling): the 131071/131072-byte boundary is the Linux MAX_ARG_STRLEN limit (32 pages = 131072 bytes including the terminating NUL), NOT a cap in the binary. q of 131071 'z' -> rc=0, verbatim, L5_len=131071. q of 131072 'z' -> execve fails with errno E2BIG 'Argument list too long', rc=127, 0 bytes of stdout, the program never runs. Same at 131073 and 200000. So: no binary-side cap exists at any reachable length.

NEW: query and fragment cannot influence lines 1-4 (scheme/host/port/path) either. The oracle asserted lines 1-4 byte-equal to the q=f="" base run on all 13,298 checks; 0 mismatches. Lines 1-4 are a pure function of argv[1..4].

NEW: query/fragment are not involved in the binary's only abort path. A port string that std::stoi cannot parse aborts before ANY output: ("http","h","abc","/",q,f) -> rc=134 (SIGABRT, core dumped), stdout 0 bytes, stderr 'terminate called after throwing an instance of std::invalid_argument / what(): stoi', identically for all 9 tested (q,f) combinations including q=f="". Query/fragment neither cause nor prevent it.

NEW: to_string appends the '?'/'#' separators blindly AFTER whatever the path dimension renders, so the final string can legitimately contain several '?' or '#'. Evidence: path=[/a?b] q=[c=d] f=[e] -> L7=[http://example.com:80/a?b?c=d#e]; path=[/a#b] -> L7=[http://example.com:80/a#b?c=d#e]; path=[?] (which path() renders as [/?]) q=[q] f=[f] -> L7=[http://example.com:80/??q#f]; path=[#] (renders as [/#]) -> L7=[http://example.com:80/#?q#f]. The 'exactly one separator added' rule is about what to_string ADDS, not about the character count of the result.

NEW (surprising literal): the base can render as the empty string while query/fragment are still appended, producing a to_string that starts with '?' or '#'. ("","example.com","-1","","","") -> L7=[] with L8=1; the same shape with q=[Q] f=[F] -> L7=[?Q#F] with L8=1. Likewise ("","","0","","Q","F") -> L7=[?Q#F] with L8=0. There is no guard suppressing query/fragment when the prefix is empty.

NEW: output is deterministic and locale-independent. Six runs of ("http","example.com","80","/","b=2&a=1&b=3","#F ?x") produced identical md5 83921f10a5fc39bea21a688d027604fd; LC_ALL/LANG in {C, en_US.UTF-8, POSIX} with q=[Q=%2f<U+65E5>] f=[F+ ] produced identical md5 edbaf86304c3ef2bad35edcc6cf1b7f5. No locale-dependent case folding or byte classification.

NEW (invocation contract detail, affects harness design): with only 5 argv values the program exits rc=1 printing nothing to stdout or stderr; with 7 it ignores the extra and behaves exactly as with 6 ('http','e','80','/','q','f','extra' -> L7=[http://e:80/?q#f], rc=0). Any test harness must therefore verify it really passed 6, since a dropped trailing empty silently yields rc=1 and no output rather than a visible error.
